title: A Tetranuclear Dysprosium Schiff Base Complex Showing Slow Relaxation of Magnetization

synthesis.procedure: A methanol solution of DyCl3·6H2O (1.0 mmol, 0.376 g) in 15 mL was slowly added to a stirring methanol solution (50 mL) of o-vanillin (1 mmol, 0.152 g) and 2-(aminomethyl)pyridine (1 mmol, 0.108 mL) in the presence of triethylamine (1 mmol, 0.101 mL). The mixture was refluxed for 4 h in an oil bath. The yellow solution was cooled to room temperature and filtered. Vapor diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate yielded yellow block crystals, which were collected by filtration, washed with cold MeOH, and dried in air and vacuum.
synthesis.temperature: reflux, then cooled to room temperature
synthesis.vessel_or_method: oil-bath reflux; diethyl ether vapor diffusion crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered; vapor diffusion of diethyl ether into the yellow filtrate gave X-ray quality yellow block crystals; collected by filtration, washed with cold MeOH, dried in air and vacuum

properties.summary: DC data show weak antiferromagnetic exchange among four Dy(III) centres. AC susceptibility is nonzero at zero DC field, establishing SMM behaviour with two (LF/HF) relaxation channels; HF relaxation below 8 K is nearly temperature-independent, consistent with QTM.
